title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Strip Bay. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Strip Bay
options.thesis: Each question is a paper strip in a bay: cited, or pulled and marked HOLD.
options.viewport: Ask fills the bay: the live strip in front, prior runs racked above it, source chosen as a labeled position.
options.risk: Turns into a toy airplane theme if the columns stop being the question, the access check, and the citation.

raised.raise: A run changes state as one physical event: the strip seats and its fields fill, never a spinner.
One vertical order rules the bay: the live strip is nearest, earlier runs sit behind it.
Source, access, and citation must agree before remarks are trusted; disagreement is HOLD.
Auto, Company documents, General, and Web are labeled positions, not mystery icons.
The live strip holds still while it is read. Only the rack behind it may shift.

options.label: Closed Stacks
options.lineage: library call slips and closed stacks
options.thesis: You file a request slip. The desk returns the passage you may see, or a refusal slip.
options.viewport: Ask is the desk: a written request, then either the returned passage with its shelf mark or a stamped refusal.
options.risk: Also the direction most evidence products land on: a polite archive template.

options.label: Graphite Panels
options.thesis: The console is persistent graphite panels. State is a syntax color. Destructive actions sit alone.
options.viewport: Ask is one panel among panels that stay put: question, run, and citation change inside the frame.
options.case: Clearer for dense tables and admin than a strip bay. Weaker identification: this is the developer console the product is leaving.
options.risk: Becomes the thin local test tool again, with amber syntax on graphite.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.viewport: A question breaks into weather and reforms as an answer landscape.
options.case: Company members do not recognize letter-weather, and a citation cannot be a storm.
options.kept: A state change is one physical event you can watch.
options.risk: The answer becomes a spectacle and the evidence disappears.

options.label: The Descent
options.lineage: a night dive down a wall
options.viewport: The question descends through depths until a lamp finds a citation.
options.case: A desk question is not a dive, and depth hides whether the caller may see the text.
options.kept: One axis orders the work, so state has a position.
options.risk: Retrieval becomes atmosphere and the refusal has nowhere to sit.

options.label: The Front Line
options.lineage: a cracktro title on a black void
options.viewport: The active question is the brightest line. Nothing is boxed.
options.case: Members do not identify with a demoscene night, and citations need a place to be read.
options.kept: The thing you are reading holds still. Motion stays behind it.
options.risk: A citation with no holder is a line you cannot inspect.

options.label: The Six-Pack
options.viewport: Six gauges agree before you trust the answer.
options.case: A cockpit is not this desk, and gauges hide the passage.
options.kept: Trust is a cross-check: source, access, and citation must agree.
options.risk: The question becomes a dial and the document never appears.

options.label: The Fascia
options.viewport: Every function is a labeled switch on one bolted panel.
options.case: A tape deck is not a reading desk, and passages do not fit a fascia.
options.kept: Every control is a labeled position you can name.
options.risk: The product becomes a prop and the evidence has no column.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A chat thread, a left rail, source chips, and a citation drawer, played straight.
canonCard.viewport: Ask is a message list. You type at the bottom. Citations open in a side drawer.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other assistant, by design.
